payload.title: aria-kernel/pyproject.toml package-data still lists the non-recursive data/*.json and data/sandbox_etc/* while the dead-wire adapter and its manifest now treat every data/**/*.json as kernel policy, so a nested policy file would be read by the adapter but absent from a packaged kernel
evidence: aria-kernel/pyproject.toml:39-40 (package-data matches data/*.json and data/sandbox_etc/* only)
tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.ts:194-199 (the policy walk collects every .json under the policy directory recursively)
tools/aria-adapters/kernel-dead-wire-adapter.test.ts:49-60 (the test fixture treats data/nested/zz.json as policy)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback.py:431 (a policy file is loaded as a package resource of aria_kernel.data, which exists only if it is packaged)
payload.rule_violated: Single owner of the policy-file surface (CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 2/3): one definition, or a test that fails when the statements diverge
payload.notes: The package now states that data/<sub>/x.json is legitimate kernel policy (manifest scope and adapter walk), but setuptools packages only data/*.json and data/sandbox_etc/*. A loader that opens such a file works from a checkout and fails on a built or installed kernel. The tree tracks no nested policy JSON today (only sandbox_etc/hosts and nsswitch.conf), so the gap is latent. Close condition: Set package-data to the same surface (data/**/*.json plus the sandbox_etc files) or derive both from one definition, and add an aria-kernel test that every tracked file under aria_kernel/data matching the adapter's policy surface is matched by a package-data pattern; closed when that test is green and goes red for a nested JSON file added without a pattern. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
